cards.text: VEL-WEEKENDER-ONEBAG-01 TWO LANE STORYBOARD

cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: The Eleanor Weekender, Light Chocolate hero. Reference adapt of an 81 second creator review that has been running 167 days. Left lane is the reference as staged, 20 scenes cut from 28 cuts. Right lane is our version, same beat functions in the same order, same cut rhythm (mean 3.0s, nothing over 4s), same energy curve, one continuous voiceover over silent b-roll with no talking head. Everything on the surface is rebuilt: their claims ladder is bolt-on features, ours is construction. Runtime about 85 seconds. Nothing renders until Brooks approves this board.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: This is the bag I wish I'd found ten years ago
CU. Modern home, terrazzo floor. Woman's torso and hands only. Dark green duffel sliding onto a matching hardshell roller handle. Locked off.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Warm, mid energy, no face

BEAT JOB: hook, retrospective verdict. Quietly demonstrates the trolley sleeve 50 seconds before it is named, so the viewer has already accepted it.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I've had expensive bags. I've had designer bags.
MS. Bedroom, patterned wallpaper. Creator (mid 40s) laying a rolled item into a light green duffel on the bed.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Reflective dip

BEAT JOB: concession. Establishes she has bought and been wrong before, which buys the verdict its credibility.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: This is the only one I actually travel with
WS. Suburban driveway, black convertible, trunk open. She lowers the duffel in beside a matching case.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Resolve

BEAT JOB: contrast resolution. The concession pays off and the verdict lands.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: It's the Weekender from Nobl
MS. Hallway, fireplace and shelving. She raises the roller handle, duffel seated on top.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Plain, matter of fact

BEAT JOB: name it. Product and brand stated flat at 9 seconds, no build up.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: so let me tell you what I actually think
CU. Outdoor bench, foliage. Light blue duffel alone, nobody in frame.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Breath, settling

BEAT JOB: breath. A product-alone static frame resets the ad before the review body starts.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: First, it fits more than it should. Three to five days, easily.
MS overhead into CU overhead. Bed. Hands push a large garment down into the bag, then the packed interior with clothes laid out beside it.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Rising competence

BEAT JOB: claim 1, capacity. Ordinal connective opens the demo stack. Two cuts, hands only.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: (zipper sound)
MS. Hands zip the duffel shut on the bed.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Punctuation

BEAT JOB: seal it. The zipper sound closes the capacity argument. The ad uses this sound three separate times as a full stop.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And it counts as a personal item, so I'm never paying baggage fees
MS tracking. Airport terminal, baggage carts behind. She pulls the duffel seated on the roller.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Satisfaction

BEAT JOB: claim 2, money. The single strongest claim in the ad and the reason it has run 167 days.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: At this point in my life, I refuse to pay for things I don't have to
WS tracking. Busy terminal, other travelers. She walks through frame.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Identity, quiet conviction

BEAT JOB: value aside. An identity line dropped mid demo that has nothing to do with the feature around it. This is the flow move worth stealing.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: The inside is thoughtfully laid out
CU overhead. Open dark green duffel, a hand pointing at interior pockets.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Instructional

BEAT JOB: interior tour. Opens the organisation block.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: There's a padded laptop pocket, which I use every trip
CU. Green armchair. Hands slide a laptop into a padded sleeve inside the bag.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Recognition

BEAT JOB: the every-trip feature. Claim and demonstration land in the same 3 seconds.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Multiple pockets that are actually where you need them
CU. Bed. Hands open and close several exterior pockets, then zip one.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Competence

BEAT JOB: pocket stack. Volume of proof rather than depth.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: My favorite feature is the bottom compartment
CU, 4.0s, the longest hold in the ad. Green armchair. A woman leans in and unzips the bottom compartment, pulls out sandals.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
PEAK. The ad slows down here

BEAT JOB: superlative pick. The only place the cutting relaxes. Announced as a favourite, not as a spec, which is why it reads as opinion rather than copy.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Shoes go in there. Toiletries go in there.
MS. Bed. She packs shoes, then toiletries, into the bottom compartment and zips it.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Held peak

BEAT JOB: proof of the pick. A repetition beat, two short parallel sentences over two actions.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: The other thing I didn't expect to love this much?
MS. Room corner, wood floor, plant. Duffel on a white roller, static, nobody in frame.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Anticipation

BEAT JOB: surprise setup. Question posed over a still product frame, answer withheld across the cut.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: The trolley sleeve. It slides right onto your carry-on handle and stays put.
WS, 4.0s, joint longest hold. Parking lot, SUV trunk open. She slides the duffel onto the handle then loads both.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Payoff

BEAT JOB: surprise payoff. Answers the question from the previous card and retroactively explains shot 1.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: No more holding a bag on your shoulder for an entire terminal. My neck and back appreciate it more than I want to admit.
WS then MS tracking. Terminal again, same staging as 0:22. She walks with the luggage.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Relief

BEAT JOB: physical relief. The most honest sentence in the ad, placed exactly where fatigue actually happens.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And honestly, it just looks good
MS. Parking lot. Duffel on a white roller, static, nobody in frame.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Lift

BEAT JOB: aesthetic pivot. Function is finished, the ad turns to how it looks.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: It looks polished enough for a work trip and casual enough for a long weekend
WS driveway (the 0:06 set reused), then WS of a woman seated on an outdoor bench with the bag.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Aspiration

BEAT JOB: dual context. One claim split across two settings so each half gets its own picture.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I've gotten compliments I didn't ask for. They're running 46% off right now. And if you buy one, you get a second free. I'm grabbing one for my sister.
Four fast cuts. Parking lot walk, then a colorway spread, then hands opening a branded box on a living room floor revealing a pink duffel.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Acquisitive warmth, closing small and intimate

BEAT JOB: social proof into offer into CTA. The discount is immediately converted into a gift, which turns a price cut into generosity. Note the ad ends small, on a box on a floor, not on a wide.

cards.title: REFERENCE CREATIVE  ·  Competitor creator review, 81.15s, 28 cuts, 167 days running. Watched frame by frame.
SCRIPT
cards.text: If you take short trips, this is the bag I would buy.
CU. Entry hall bench, morning light through a doorway. Her hands only, setting the closed Light Chocolate Weekender down beside a carry-on. Front on, locked off, no camera move.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Warm, mid energy, no face. Same register as the reference hook.

BEAT JOB: hook, flat verdict before the product is named. PRODUCT TRUTH: closed and unfastened is the as-filmed default state, flap down, belt straps hanging near the SIDE edges with their gold end plates visible, staples exposed. Scale is critical, the bag is 18 inches wide, it reads as a carry-on duffel and not a handbag. PROMPT SKETCH: an ordinary iPhone snapshot, slightly off centre, of two hands lowering a large structured cream canvas and cognac leather weekend bag onto a wooden entry bench next to a small rolling carry-on, one dominant window light, real shadows, nothing tack sharp.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I have bought a lot of bags. Most of them are still sitting in my closet.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: MS. Bedroom, unmade bed, an open wardrobe visible behind her with other bags on the shelf. Creator (one woman, mid 40s, locked as the same person in every shot) lays a folded stack down beside the open bag.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Reflective dip, exactly where the reference dips.

BEAT JOB: concession. Her own buying history, no judgement on anything she bought. LAW: no villain, no competitor, no other bag is criticised in frame or in line. PROMPT SKETCH: candid handheld frame of a woman in her mid forties in a real bedroom placing folded clothes beside a large open weekend bag on the bed, other handbags visible on a wardrobe shelf behind her, available light only.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: This is the one that actually leaves the house with me.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: WS. Driveway, car trunk open. She lowers the packed bag in beside a carry-on. Static camera, she moves.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Resolve. The verdict lands.

BEAT JOB: contrast resolution, the concession pays off. CARRY LAW: the bag is held by both rolled handles in her hand, never on a shoulder. Reaches from her hip toward her knee. PROMPT SKETCH: a real snapshot of a woman lowering a large cognac and cream weekend bag into an open car trunk in a suburban driveway, flat daylight, slightly crooked framing.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: It is the Eleanor Weekender from Velantra, and I have had it a year.
MS. Hall or entry. She lifts the bag onto her forearm and turns it front on to the lens.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Plain and matter of fact, no salesmanship.

BEAT JOB: name it. Brand and product stated flat at 9 seconds, mirroring the reference exactly. AUDIO: Weekender is said WEEK-en-der, three syllables, sound the D. Never render the word Weekender as engine text, caption overlays only. SCALE: as wide as her shoulders, both forearms underneath. PROMPT SKETCH: handheld frame of a woman turning a large structured weekend bag front on toward the camera in a real hallway, held on her forearm, hardware large and sharply lit in frame.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So here is what I actually think.
CU. Closed bag alone on a stone bench outdoors, morning light, straps hanging, nobody in frame. Slow handheld drift.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Breath, settling before the review body.

BEAT JOB: breath. SOURCE: real 4K footage IMG_4049, no generation needed. This card is the reference's product-alone reset beat, kept exactly.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: First, it holds more than it looks like it should. 3 days of clothes.
Two cuts. MS overhead of hands pressing a folded stack down into the open bag, then CU overhead of the packed interior with the rest of the pile beside it.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Rising competence.

BEAT JOB: claim 1, capacity, opened with the same ordinal connective as the reference. PRODUCT TRUTH: live PDP reads Packs 2 to 3 day trips. The line stays at 3 days and no higher. Interior lining material is deliberately not claimed, see the notes below. SOURCE: real packed b-roll.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: No zipper on it anywhere. The whole flap folds down in one piece.
MS. Hands fold the one-piece cognac leather flap down over the packed bag, the gold oval plate settling over the knurled post.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Punctuation. The soft sound of leather and the click of the plate replace the reference's zipper.

BEAT JOB: seal it. THIS IS THE KEY REDIRECT. The reference zips here and twice more. Our bag has no zipper at all, so the flap does the closing and the absence becomes the claim. SOURCE: real footage IMG_4051 played in reverse. Never ask an engine to animate the closure.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Packed full it still goes in the overhead bin, so I am not checking a bag.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: MS. Airport, the bag lifts into an overhead bin, hands release, the door shuts.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Satisfaction.

BEAT JOB: claim, money. WHAT WE CANNOT SAY: the reference claims a personal item and no baggage fees. At 18 inches wide this is a carry-on, not a personal item, and claiming otherwise becomes a support ticket. Overhead bin is live PDP copy and is what we say. HIGHEST GENERATION RISK BEAT: 3 variants, pick clean, frame QA against the closed hero. If all 3 fail, cut it and run about 83 seconds.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: At this point I would rather buy one good bag and keep it for 10 years.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: WS tracking. Airport concourse. She walks, bag carried in her hand at her side, reaching from hip toward knee.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Identity, quiet conviction. The reference's best flow move, ported.

BEAT JOB: value aside, dropped mid demo and unrelated to the feature around it. This carries the brand spine (timelessness, a bag you keep) into the money slot. CARRY LAW: hand or forearm only, the handles physically cannot reach a shoulder.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Inside is one open space with a wide leather slip pocket.
CU overhead. Open bag on a chair, her hand holding the mouth open and indicating the slip pocket down the interior wall.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Instructional.

BEAT JOB: interior tour. PRODUCT TRUTH CONFLICT, RESOLVED: the live product page says the lining is natural cotton canvas, the 8/08 footage of the physical bag shows smooth caramel leather. The script claims only the leather slip pocket, which both sources agree on, and never names the lining material. SOURCE: real footage, never generated.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: My laptop goes in flat against it.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: CU. A laptop slides in flat against the slip pocket wall, all the way down.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Recognition.

BEAT JOB: the every-trip demo, same slot as the reference's laptop pocket. WHAT WE CANNOT SAY: we have no padded laptop pocket. The laptop still goes in and we show it going in, so the demo survives and the claim shrinks to what is true. SOURCE: real footage.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: The turn lock actually works. You twist the post and the straps hook over.
Two macro cuts. A real hand twists the knurled gold post, then a strap tip plate hooks over its staple.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Competence, material forensics.

BEAT JOB: takes the pocket-stack slot. We have no exterior pockets, so the hardware does the work. PRODUCT TRUTH: one knurled mushroom-head post at front centre of the band, two flat vertical gold staples either side each made of two parallel bars, the single oval keyhole plate lives on the flap tab and appears exactly once on the bag. Working gold turn-lock is live PDP copy. SOURCE: real footage IMG_4052 and IMG_4050. Never generated, this is where engines invent three different lock geometries in one ad.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: My favorite thing is the flap. It folds all the way back and the whole top opens at once.
CU, 4.0s, the longest hold in our cut, matching the reference. One take of the one-piece flap folding all the way back and the caramel interior opening.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
PEAK. The cutting relaxes here and nowhere else.

BEAT JOB: superlative pick, announced as a favourite rather than a spec. This is our strongest owned fact and it takes the exact slot their bottom compartment held. SOURCE: real footage IMG_4051, one continuous take. LAW: no engine ever animates the bag opening. Fail on sight if any frame shows a flap-shaped panel left on the front, a split flap, or any zipper.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Shoes in the bottom, toiletries on top, and I can reach any of it without unpacking.
Two cuts. Shoes laid flat in the bottom, then a small pouch set on top of them and her hand reaching past it to pull something out.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Held peak.

BEAT JOB: proof of the pick, the reference's repetition beat with the parallel echo softened into one sentence. PROP NOTE: if a toiletry pouch is in frame, the only zipper in the entire scene belongs to that pouch. The bag has none. SOURCE: real packed b-roll.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: What I did not expect to care about is how it holds its shape,
MS. The closed bag standing on its own on the floor by the door, static, nobody in frame.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Anticipation.

BEAT JOB: surprise setup. The sentence deliberately runs across the cut and finishes on the next card, exactly the way the reference splits its trolley sleeve question and answer. SOURCE: real footage IMG_4049.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: packed full or barely packed at all.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: MS, 4.0s, joint longest hold. She sets the packed bag down and it stands upright on its own, hard cut, she sets it down nearly empty and it holds the same shape.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Payoff.

BEAT JOB: surprise payoff, in the trolley sleeve slot. Keeps its shape packed full or barely at all is live PDP copy, quoted almost verbatim. This is also the direct answer to the loudest structural objection in the VoC (slouches wayyy too much once you put anything in it). SOURCE: real footage, two setups.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: The handles are rolled leather and sit on my forearm, so my hands are free.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Two cuts. Airport, forearm carry with a coffee and a boarding pass in the free hand, then a tracking shot down the concourse with the same carry.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Relief.

BEAT JOB: physical relief, in the same slot as the reference's neck and back line. CARRY LAW, NON NEGOTIABLE: short rolled top handles reach a hand or a forearm and nothing else. Never stage or prompt a shoulder carry, and never let an engine invent a long buckled shoulder strap. If an engine cannot hold a walking carry, these become locked stills.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And honestly, it just looks like a nice bag.
MS. The bag resting on top of the carry-on outdoors, static, nobody in frame.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Lift. Function is finished, the ad turns to how it looks.

BEAT JOB: aesthetic pivot, on the same And honestly connective the reference uses. SOURCE: real footage IMG_4049.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: No logo anywhere, inside or out, and the leather has softened where I hold it.
Two cuts. A push across the clean front band and the plain back band, then a macro of the softened creased leather where the handle base meets the band.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Discernment.

BEAT JOB: takes the dual-context slot. PRODUCT TRUTH: no logos, stamps or embossing anywhere outside or inside, confirmed on the physical bag. The back band is plain, two teardrop handle bases only, no lock and no staples. The patina line is the brand's timelessness proof. SOURCE: real footage.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: People ask where it is from, and no one ever guesses. It has a 2 year warranty, and if something goes wrong they replace it. Right now they are running 50 dollars off. I am getting the army green one for my mom. Link is below.

Four fast cuts. Creator seated on a bench with the bag beside her and a passerby glancing at it, then a 3 way colorway spread at 0.8s each (Light Chocolate, Army Green, Dark Chocolate), then a screen recording of the live product page with 159.99 struck from 209.99, then she hands the Army Green bag to an older woman in a doorway.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Acquisitive warmth, closing small and intimate on the handover, mirroring the reference's close on a box on a floor.

BEAT JOB: social proof into warranty into offer into CTA. OFFER VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-03: 209.99 struck to 159.99, save 50.00. WARRANTY: two years, free replacement rather than repair, running from delivery. NO COLORWAY COUNT IN THE VOICEOVER: the fourth colorway is on pre-order for mid September 2026 and a pre-order claim requires a stated ship date, so the count is dropped and only the three shipping colors appear on screen. The gift close carries the hand-down spine instead of the reference's buy-one-get-one.

cards.title: OUR VERSION  ·  VEL-WEEKENDER-ONEBAG-01. The Eleanor Weekender, Light Chocolate. Angle VEL-A-002, the compromise trip bag. About 85 seconds, 20 scenes, 28 cuts, one continuous voiceover.

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: APPROVAL GATE
cards.text: Nothing renders, animates or generates until Brooks approves this board. Approve or redirect four things: the angle (VEL-A-002, the compromise trip bag), the script as written, the 20 scene structure, and the casting call in the next note.

cards.title: CASTING
cards.text: One creator, one woman, mid 40s, locked as the same reference in every shot she appears in. The reference ad used three different women and five colorways because it is stitched from affiliate footage. We do not copy that. Light Chocolate is the hero in every scene except the colorway spread and the handover.

cards.title: STRUCTURE
cards.text: One continuous voiceover across the full 85 seconds, never spliced per beat, and no talking head anywhere. The reference has no on-camera speech either, and that is the single most useful structural fact the watch turned up.

cards.title: WHAT WAS KEPT
cards.text: All 20 beat functions in their original order. The cut rhythm: 28 cuts, mean 3.0 seconds, nothing over 4 seconds, the two longest holds reserved for the superlative pick and the surprise payoff. The energy curve including the reflective dip at 3 to 9 seconds and the small intimate close. The shot grammar: hands-only macro for every claim, wide for every transport beat, product-alone statics as breath beats.

cards.title: SCRIPT FLOW PORTED
cards.text: The retrospective verdict opener, the concession and its resolution, the flat product naming, the permission line, the ordinal connective, the value aside dropped mid demo, the superlative announced as a favourite, the setup and payoff split across a cut, the And honestly pivot, unasked-for social proof, the offer stated once with no adjectives, and the personal gift close.

cards.title: WHAT WAS REBUILT
cards.text: Their claims ladder is bolt-on features: a trolley sleeve, a padded laptop pocket, a sealed shoe compartment, a personal-item fee dodge. Every rung is something a competitor could add next season. Ours is construction: no zipper anywhere, a one-piece flap that folds all the way back, a working gold turn post with two belt straps hooking over staple plates, rolled handles that only reach a forearm, no logo inside or out, holds its shape packed or empty.

cards.title: SWAP TEST
cards.text: Drop the reference's own bag into our script and it fails at the no-zipper line, the turn post, the fold-back flap, the forearm-only handles and the no-logo claim. Five of six construction lines break. The angle cannot be lifted by anyone else.

cards.title: SIX MONTH TEST
cards.text: No season, no holiday, no calendar beat anywhere in the script. Short trips and a long weekend are permanent categories. The only dated line is the offer, which swaps when the sale does.

cards.title: PRODUCT TRUTH, VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-03
cards.text: The Eleanor Weekender, 209.99 struck to 159.99. Approx 18 inches wide by 14.5 high by 7 deep. Packs 2 to 3 day trips, fits the overhead bin, keeps its shape packed full or barely at all, working gold turn-lock, leather slip pocket, two year warranty. Colorways: Light Chocolate, Army Green, Dark Chocolate, and Black on pre-order for mid September 2026.

cards.title: OPEN CONFLICT FOR BROOKS
cards.text: The live product page describes the interior as natural cotton-canvas lining. The 8/08 footage of the physical bag shows a smooth caramel leather lining with a matching caramel slip pocket, and the product record already corrected that canvas description once as an error. The script sidesteps it by claiming only the leather slip pocket and never naming the lining material, but the product page copy should be fixed either way.

cards.title: PRODUCTION LAWS
cards.text: Real 4K product footage carries every beat where the hardware or the interior is large in frame. Never regenerate what was already filmed. No engine animates the bag being opened, unfastened, or carried while walking. No shoulder carry anywhere. Captions burn from the script, never from ASR, and the word Weekender never renders as engine text.

cards.title: ONLY REAL GENERATION RISK
cards.text: The overhead bin beat at 0:22. Three variants, pick clean, frame QA against the closed hero before anything animates. If all three fail, cut the beat and the ad runs about 83 seconds. Everything else is either real footage or a simple staged beat with no hand on the hardware.
MOODBOARD
Default closed state, flap down, straps hanging near the side edges
The one-piece fold-back flap and the caramel interior. Our superlative beat
Hardware truth: knurled post, oval keyhole plate, staples
Scale anchor. An adult hand spans a fraction of the front
Army Green, the colorway in the gift close
